environment.description: Same Actix-web binary deployed on ECS Fargate behind an ALB with two layered controls: (1) An ALB listener rule with a fixed-response action that strips and regenerates the 'session_token' form field by injecting a Lambda@Edge-equivalent ALB action (using ALB's advanced request routing with a condition on the POST body pattern matching 'session_token=' followed by a non-empty value, returning HTTP 400 before reaching the target group), and (2) a Cloudfront distribution in front of the ALB with a Response Headers Policy that enforces 'Content-Security-Policy: require-sri-for script style; default-src self' on ALL responses, which means any attacker-injected script (e.g., via XSS to deliver the fixation link with a crafted token) would be blocked unless it passes SRI validation. The CloudFront distribution also sets 'Clear-Site-Data: cookies' header on any response from /login path when a query string contains 'token=', effectively destroying any pre-set session cookie before the login form renders.

config.load_balancer: AWS ALB with advanced request routing rules
config.alb_rule_1: Condition: HttpRequestMethod=POST AND Path=/auth/login AND body contains non-empty session_token field → fixed-response 400
config.cloudfront: Distribution with Response Headers Policy ID rp-658327ab
config.cloudfront_csp: require-sri-for script style; default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' https://cdn.example.com
config.cloudfront_behavior_login: Path pattern /login* with query string 'token' present → inject Clear-Site-Data: "cookies" response header
config.network: private subnet, ALB in public subnet, no direct instance access
config.sri_enforcement: Browser-enforced via CSP require-sri-for directive on all page loads
